stem: A grocery chain wants to stop discovering empty shelves only when customers complain. Leaders want store managers to see sales and stock movements as they happen so replenishment can be ordered the same day. Which business value of data does this goal illustrate?

choices.text: Lowering hardware spending, so that the chain can retire a few older servers in its head-office building
Generating real-time business insights, so that managers can act on events while they are still happening
Archiving records for later audits, so that the chain can prove what was sold once each year has closed
Standardizing store layouts, so that every outlet displays the same products in the same positions

stem: An insurer's executives are surprised that a pilot AI claims assistant gives vague and sometimes wrong answers. The assistant was built quickly, but the claims records it learns from are scattered across departments, partly outdated and inconsistently labeled. Which statement best explains the situation in terms of the role of data?

choices.text: AI replaces the need for data, so the answers should have been correct even though the records were scattered and outdated
Data volume alone decides AI quality, so adding more outdated records from other departments would fix the answers
Data fuels AI, so the quality, completeness and accessibility of the data behind a model strongly shape how good its results are
Data matters only for reporting, so the pilot's weak answers must come from the interface the claims staff use

stem: A retail bank runs an application where customers transfer money. Each transfer must be recorded immediately and correctly, and thousands of such small updates happen every minute. Separately, the finance team wants to analyze years of combined data from many systems for reports. Which pairing matches these two needs?

choices.text: A database for the transfers, and a second copy of that same database for the cross-system reporting
A data warehouse for the transfers, and a database for the cross-system reporting
A data lake for the transfers, and a database for the cross-system reporting
A database for the transfers, and a data warehouse for the cross-system reporting

stem: A streaming company collects clickstream logs, video thumbnails, support-call recordings and sensor files. Its data scientists do not yet know what questions they will ask, and they want the original raw data kept as it arrived so they can experiment with machine learning later. Which approach fits best?

choices.text: A data lake, which stores large amounts of data of all types in its native format without a predefined schema
A traditional on-premises warehouse that accepts only cleaned and structured tables from a nightly batch load
A transactional database with a fixed schema, so that every file is converted into rows before it is stored
A spreadsheet shared by the data scientists, where each file type is summarized into columns by hand

stem: A leadership team is deciding how to describe the difference between a data warehouse and a data lake to the board. Which TWO statements are accurate? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A data warehouse stores only video and images, while a data lake stores only numeric tables
A data lake and a data warehouse can never be used in the same company because their data cannot be combined
A data lake always requires every record to be fully cleaned and modeled before any data can be stored in it
A data lake can keep raw structured, semi-structured and unstructured data in its native format for analytics and ML
A data warehouse is optimized for repeatable business reporting and structured SQL analysis of cleaned data

stem: A furniture retailer wants to personalize its newsletter using the purchase history, website browsing behavior and loyalty-program sign-ups that it collects directly from its own customers. How is this data classified?

choices.text: First-party data, because the retailer collected it itself from its own customers and channels
Third-party data, because it describes people and so must come from an outside data aggregator
Public data, because anyone browsing the retailer's website could in principle see all of it
Second-party data, because it is about customers who each belong to a different retailer

stem: A hotel group and an airline agree to exchange anonymized booking data about travelers who have opted in to partner offers, so that each can design joint travel packages. From the hotel group's point of view, the data it receives from the airline is which kind?

choices.text: Third-party data, because the airline is another company and not the hotel group's customer
Second-party data, because it is the airline's own first-party data shared directly under a partnership agreement
Unstructured data, because exchanged booking data has no defined fields and cannot be analyzed by query
First-party data, because the hotel group now holds the records inside its own storage

stem: A marketing director wants to reach people who are not yet customers. The agency suggests buying an audience list of demographics and interests that a data aggregator compiled from many sources and sells to many advertisers. What kind of data is this, and what should the director weigh?

choices.text: First-party data, so the director can assume it is accurate because it is held in company records
Structured data only, so the director needs no checks because every field has a fixed meaning and format
Third-party data, so the director should weigh how accurate, consented and relevant it is, since the buyer did not collect it
Second-party data, so the director can expect it to be exclusive because only one partner supplied it

stem: A logistics company receives shipment events as JSON messages. Each message has labeled fields such as "shipmentId" and "status", but different carriers add different extra fields, and there is no single fixed table design. How is this data best described?

choices.text: Structured data, because a labeled field in a message proves that the data belongs in fixed rows and columns
Unstructured data, because anything that arrives as text messages carries no recognizable organization
Semi-structured data, because it has labels and organization but does not follow a rigid, fixed table schema
Unlabeled data, because the extra carrier fields mean that nobody tagged the data with the correct outcome

stem: A city transport authority wants to map its data supply chain. It starts with the moment a passenger taps a card on a bus reader, which creates a travel record that did not exist before. Which stage of the data supply chain is this?

choices.text: Data analysis, the point at which people or systems examine data to find patterns and answers
Data activation, the point at which insights are put to work in an action, product or process
Data processing, the point at which raw records are cleaned and transformed into a more useful form
Data genesis, the point at which data is first created or generated by an event, device or interaction

stem: A manufacturer's dashboards show inflated production counts. An investigation finds that sensor readings reach the central system correctly but include duplicates, readings in different units and missing values, and nothing fixes these before the data is stored. At which stage of the data supply chain is the gap, and what does it call for?

choices.text: Data processing, which needs cleaning, de-duplication and standardization before the data is stored and analyzed
Data collection, which needs the readings to be delayed so that they arrive less often at the central system
Data activation, which needs the dashboards redesigned so that managers see fewer production counts
Data genesis, which needs the sensors replaced so that the readings are never created in the first place

stem: A telecom company's analysts have built a model that predicts which subscribers are likely to cancel. The company now wants the call-center system to automatically show an agent a retention offer whenever a flagged subscriber phones in. Which data supply chain stage does this represent?

choices.text: Data analysis, where the model is trained and the cancellation predictions are first produced from the history
Data activation, where analytical results are fed into a business process or customer experience to drive action
Data collection, where call events are first gathered and brought in from the telephone system
Data storage, where the subscriber history is kept in a system that the analysts are able to query

stem: A bank describes its data supply chain activities. Which TWO of the following correctly pair an activity with its stage? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A customer opening a new savings account, which creates a brand-new record in the system, is data analysis
Building a dashboard of last quarter's loan trends is data collection
Loading daily branch transactions into a data warehouse for analysts to query is data storage
Cleaning mismatched date formats across the bank's regional systems is data genesis
Sending a list of high-value customers to the email platform for a targeted campaign is data activation

stem: A multinational has analysts in different countries who each keep their own copies of customer data in separate tools. They disagree on revenue totals, nobody is sure who may see personal data, and a regulator has asked how the company controls sensitive records. Which approach addresses all three problems?

choices.text: Data governance: shared standards for how data is gathered, defined, accessed, protected and used throughout its life cycle
Data deletion: removing all customer records so that no one is able to see personal data
Data hoarding: keeping every copy that each team has made, so that no team ever has to give up its own version
Data duplication: giving every analyst a private copy so that nobody depends on another team's version

stem: A company's leaders are debating whether to fund data governance, because some executives see it as only slowing teams down. Which TWO benefits of governance should the data leader cite? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A requirement that all data be stored in a single location regardless of regulations
Removal of the need for any data catalog, labeling or ownership of data
Guaranteed elimination of every security incident without any further technical controls
Safer self-service access, so more analysts can use governed data without exposing sensitive records
Trustworthy, high-quality data that reduces unreliable insights and AI answers

stem: A software company stores its analytical data in a proprietary format that only its current vendor's engine can read. Moving to a different engine would require rewriting and re-exporting years of tables. Leaders want a data platform that avoids this lock-in. Which approach reflects Google Cloud's openness?

choices.text: Keeping the proprietary format but adding another vendor's license to use as a backup in a future migration
Storing data in open table formats, such as Apache Iceberg, so that multiple engines can analyze the same data
Allowing only one approved engine for the whole company so that nobody ever needs to ask about moving
Converting all data to image files so that no analytics engine in particular is able to depend on it

stem: After acquiring two companies, a retailer finds sales data in one cloud, customer data in an on-premises system and product data in a third vendor's service. Reports need weeks of manual exports because the systems cannot share data easily. Which design principle best addresses this problem going forward?

choices.text: Standardizing on one closed ecosystem, so that every future acquisition must first rebuild its data in the vendor's format
Interoperability through open standards and connectors, so data can move and be queried across systems without manual copying
Isolation of each system, so that every department keeps strict control over its own data and rarely shares it
Printing the weekly reports from each system, so that employees can combine the results by hand

stem: A publisher's board asks why it should invest in a central data platform when editors already trust their instincts about which stories readers like. The data lead wants an argument based on identifying trends and informing strategic decisions. Which response fits?

choices.text: A central platform is valuable mainly because it prevents anyone outside the editorial team from ever viewing any readership figure
Reader data should be collected only for legal record keeping, since it cannot influence which stories the publisher chooses to commission
Editors' instincts are always more accurate than readership data, so the platform would be used mainly to store their conclusions
Analyzing reading behavior across years and topics can reveal trends, such as rising interest in a subject, so that investment decisions rest on evidence

stem: A hospital network's operations director receives a weekly dashboard showing admissions, average stay and bed occupancy by site. She asks a colleague which term describes the practice of turning this historical data into charts and reports that managers read to monitor the business. Which term is correct?

choices.text: Business intelligence, which presents historical and current data in dashboards and reports to support monitoring and decisions
Machine learning training, which adjusts a model's internal parameters until it predicts bed occupancy without any reports
Data ingestion, which moves records from source systems into storage but does not present or analyze them for managers
Generative AI, which creates new text, images or code in response to prompts written by the managers who read the reports

stem: A retailer has two requests. Team X wants a score for each customer showing the likelihood that the customer will stop buying in the next quarter, based on past behavior. Team Y wants first drafts of personalised marketing emails for each customer segment. Which pairing of AI approaches fits?

choices.text: Team X and Team Y both need predictive ML, because generative AI cannot produce text for marketing purposes
Team X needs a business intelligence dashboard to predict churn, and Team Y needs predictive ML to draft the emails
Team X needs predictive machine learning trained on past behavior, and Team Y needs generative AI that creates new text
Team X needs generative AI to write the score, and Team Y needs a rule-based system with fixed email templates

stem: A software company says its sales organisation is changing because AI agents now research each prospect, draft outreach, update the customer record and schedule follow-ups, with sellers reviewing the results. Which description best captures what makes this agentic AI different from a conventional chatbot?

choices.text: The assistant is given a goal, plans several steps, uses connected tools and business systems to act, and returns results for review
The assistant stores sales notes in a database and shows them on a dashboard that sellers must update by hand
The assistant only answers one question at a time from a fixed script and waits for the seller to do every follow-up step
The assistant is a model that is retrained each night on seller activity so that its forecasts become slightly more accurate

stem: A telecom provider introduces AI agents in customer support. The agents resolve many billing and plan-change requests end to end by using internal systems. Leaders want the productivity gain but are worried that an agent could take a wrong action on a customer account. Which approach balances value and risk best?

choices.text: Keep the agents read-only forever so that they only suggest answers, and humans make every change to every customer account
Give the agents narrow permissions, require human approval for sensitive actions, and monitor results as scope grows
Replace all human support staff with the agents at once, so that no one is needed to review exceptions
Let the agents act freely on every account in the first week, and rely on customers to report mistakes by phone

stem: A bank with decades of transaction data in BigQuery wants to build AI features. Its CIO says the main benefit of choosing Google Cloud for this plan is that AI can work where the data already lives, instead of the bank copying data between separate analytics and AI systems. Which Google Cloud AI benefit is the CIO describing?

choices.text: Best infrastructure for AI, where the benefit is chiefly the supply of custom chips for training large models
Sophisticated first-party models, where the benefit is chiefly a model that Google developed itself
An AI-ready data cloud, where analytics and AI services work directly on the data in the same platform
Pre-built agents and applications, where employees receive finished tools and the bank's data plays no role

stem: A professional-services firm wants every employee to get AI help with summarising documents, drafting messages and automating routine tasks within weeks, and it has no AI engineering team. Select TWO Google Cloud AI benefits that most directly match this goal. (Select TWO)

choices.text: A requirement to develop and train a custom foundation model first, so that the answers reflect the firm's voice
A data warehouse migration that must finish before any employee can use an AI assistant for documents
Best infrastructure for AI, which lets the firm design its own accelerator hardware layout for training
Agents grounded in enterprise data, which answer from the firm's own repositories rather than only from general knowledge
Pre-built AI agents and applications, which employees use without building models or writing code

stem: A card issuer's fraud team maintains thousands of hand-written rules such as "flag purchases over a set amount abroad". Fraudsters keep finding gaps, and each new pattern takes weeks to encode. Legitimate customers are also blocked by overly broad rules. Which business benefit of machine learning addresses these problems?

choices.text: ML makes the rules human-readable in a dashboard, so analysts can edit each of them more quickly than before
ML guarantees that fraud will no longer occur, so the fraud team and any review process can be removed
ML stores the existing rules more efficiently, so that the thousands of rules can be evaluated faster at the same accuracy as today
ML learns patterns from labelled past transactions, adapts to new behavior and reduces both missed fraud and false blocks

stem: An insurer has years of claim records in tables, plus millions of adjuster notes, accident photos and recorded calls that analysts have never been able to use because they cannot be searched with ordinary queries. Which business value does machine learning, including gen AI, add here?

choices.text: It makes the tables more accurate by deleting every record that does not contain a photo or an audio file
It removes the need to keep the original claim files and recordings, since the model can reproduce each of them exactly whenever needed
It turns the unstructured notes, photos and audio into information that can be analyzed with the structured claim data
It lets the insurer avoid defining a business question, since the model finds a useful objective on its own

stem: A bank wants to send each of its millions of customers a relevant product offer every month. Today, analysts segment customers by hand into a few groups, which is slow and treats very different customers alike. Which statement describes how ML helps the bank scale this decision?

choices.text: ML sends the offers itself without any data, because it infers customer interests from the bank's name alone
ML scores each customer's likely interest automatically, so offers can be personalised at a scale analysts cannot reach by hand
ML makes one decision for the whole customer base, which saves the cost of evaluating individual customers
ML produces a much larger number of hand-written segments, which analysts then maintain for each customer group separately

stem: A city utility wants software that computes each household's water bill. The calculation follows a published tariff table: a fixed charge plus set rates per usage band. Auditors require that identical readings always give identical bills. A consultant proposes training a machine learning model on past bills. What should a business leader conclude?

choices.text: Ordinary rules-based software fits, because the logic is known and must be exact and repeatable, so ML adds risk without value
A model is better because it will find a fairer tariff than the published table by learning the patterns found in past bills
A model should be trained on the auditors' comments, so that it learns which readings they will accept
A model is required because any calculation that touches millions of households must use machine learning

stem: A hospital's analytics team wants to train a model that predicts which patients are likely to be readmitted. They find that the allergy and medication-history fields are blank for a large share of patient records, although the values that are present look reasonable. Which data-quality dimension is the main problem?

choices.text: Timeliness, because the records were not updated within the expected time window
Completeness, because required information is missing from many records
Uniqueness, because the same patient appears more than once in the table
Validity, because the values present do not follow the required format or range

stem: A retailer's loyalty database shows 12,000 more members than the company believes it has. Analysis finds that customers who signed up in store and again online were stored as separate people, and the same person is counted several times in campaign reports. Which data-quality dimension is violated?

choices.text: Completeness, because required customer fields have no value in a large share of records
Consistency, because two different systems report different revenue totals for the same product
Uniqueness, because the same customer is recorded more than once and is counted repeatedly
Accuracy, because every record's values are wrong and no customer information can be trusted

stem: A logistics company's delivery-time model recommends routes using traffic and stock data that arrives in a nightly batch. Dispatchers complain that suggestions rely on road conditions from the previous day and miss current closures. Every value in the data is correct for the time it was recorded. Which data-quality dimension is the main issue?

choices.text: Timeliness, because the data is not recent enough for the decisions it supports
Accuracy, because the nightly values were incorrect when the system recorded them
Uniqueness, because road closures are listed again each night for each affected route
Validity, because the traffic values do not follow an accepted format or numeric range

stem: An HR analytics team loads employee records for a retention model. The data includes birth dates entered as text like "31-12-1985" in some rows and "1985/12/31" in others, and a few ages of -4 and 212. Which data-quality dimension do these defects most directly violate?

choices.text: Uniqueness, because several employees have identical birth years
Completeness, because the birth date column has no cells without a value
Timeliness, because dates from earlier years are older than recently entered ones
Validity, because values break the required date format and acceptable range

stem: A product-catalog table lists one SKU's colour as "Teal", which is an allowed value in the colour field and is spelled and formatted correctly. The physical product is actually orange, and customers return it. Which statement about this data is correct?

choices.text: It is both valid and accurate, because the data passed automatic format checks when it was loaded
It is accurate but not valid, because the value matches the product but breaks the field's allowed list
It is neither valid nor accurate, because every wrong value must also break a format or range check
It is valid but not accurate, because the value follows the field's rules yet does not match reality

stem: A manufacturer's finance report shows revenue for a product line that is higher than the figure in the sales team's database, even though both systems are fed by the same orders. The CFO's data team finds both numbers are internally well formed and current, yet they disagree. Which data-quality dimension is violated?

choices.text: Uniqueness, because each order is stored once in finance and once in sales
Consistency, because the same fact has different values in different systems
Validity, because a revenue figure cannot be read unless it follows a single numeric format
Completeness, because the finance report lacks the order rows needed to reach the sales figure

stem: A company's first AI pilot, a model to predict equipment failures, produced unreliable results. The review found sensor data with missing values, duplicated readings and conflicting units across plants. Select TWO statements that correctly explain why high-quality data is essential for AI. (Select TWO)

choices.text: Data quality matters only for reporting, because a model automatically corrects bad data during training
Data quality is the responsibility of the model vendor, so a company using managed AI services can ignore it
Models learn patterns from their training data, so errors and gaps in the data are learned and reproduced in predictions
A larger volume of poor data always outweighs the problems, because more rows give a model a clearer pattern
Investing in data quality up front raises trust in results and reduces rework and wasted effort after deployment

stem: A lender uses an ML model to approve or decline consumer loans. A declined applicant asks why, and regulators ask the lender to show that decisions are not based on improper factors. Which business benefit of explainable AI addresses these needs?

choices.text: It shows which inputs drove each decision, so the lender can justify outcomes to customers and regulators and spot bias
It increases the number of loans approved, because explained decisions are always more favorable to the applicants concerned
It removes the need for human oversight, because an explained decision is automatically a correct decision
It makes the model faster, because explanation replaces the calculation that the model would otherwise perform

stem: A health insurer is deciding whether to invest in responsible AI practices such as bias testing, transparency, privacy protection and human oversight before launching a claims-triage model. Select TWO business implications that support doing so. (Select TWO)

choices.text: Responsible AI is a purely technical setting in the model that only data scientists need to understand or own
Practices such as documentation, fairness testing and oversight help the insurer meet regulatory and audit expectations
Adopting responsible AI guarantees that the model will have no errors, so ongoing monitoring can stop at launch
Responsible AI practices remove all regulatory requirements, so legal review of the model is no longer needed
Reducing the chance of harmful or biased outcomes protects customers and the insurer's reputation and trust

stem: A pharmaceutical company's research group spends months reading papers, trial reports and internal notes before each new study. Leaders hear that agentic AI is changing research and product innovation and ask what an agent could change for this group. Which outcome is the most realistic?

choices.text: An agent only stores the papers in a shared folder, which scientists must still read themselves one document at a time
An agent replaces the scientists' judgement entirely, approving which compounds go to trials without any expert review
An agent guarantees that every hypothesis it proposes will succeed, so the group can skip laboratory validation steps
An agent gathers and summarises the relevant literature and internal data, proposes hypotheses, and scientists then evaluate them

stem: A media company trains and serves very large models and finds that its on-premises servers cannot scale, and training times slow its product plans. Which Google Cloud AI benefit answers this specific problem?

choices.text: Pre-built agents and applications, which supply finished employee tools but do not provide compute for training the company's models
A data-quality scorecard, which grades the company's tables but does not provide compute for training or serving models
Purpose-built AI infrastructure, with accelerators such as TPUs and GPUs, that can be scaled up as training and serving demand changes
Business intelligence dashboards, which present trained-model results to managers but do not provide compute for training

stem: A hospital group is planning its move to the cloud. The project lead lists the patient-scheduling system, the billing database and the imaging archive as three separate items to be moved, assessed and sequenced independently. What is the common term for each of these items?

choices.text: A workload, meaning an application or service together with the resources and data it needs to run
A landing zone, meaning the one-time network that must exist before any application can be moved
A region, meaning a geographic location where cloud resources are physically hosted
A tenant, meaning a separate customer account that Google creates inside the hospital's environment

stem: A manufacturer has 400 applications in two data centers. Nobody has a complete list of which systems talk to which, who owns them, or how heavily they are used. The CIO wants to avoid surprises after the move starts. Which first phase of a migration addresses this?

choices.text: Rehosting every application in one weekend, so that the old data centers can be closed before the dependencies matter
Reimagining the business model first, because the list of applications changes entirely once new products are chosen
Replatforming each application to a managed service, then documenting its dependencies afterward from the new environment
Discovery and assessment, which inventories the workloads and their dependencies and evaluates how each should be migrated

stem: During migration planning, a bank finds a reporting application that nobody has opened in two years. Its former users moved to a newer analytics tool. How should this workload be handled in the migration plan?

choices.text: Refactored into microservices so that, if the users ever return, the application is ready for a modern platform
Retained on premises indefinitely, because applications that nobody uses are always the safest to leave untouched
Retired, which means decommissioning it so that no money or effort is spent moving or running it
Rehosted to virtual machines in the cloud so that its current appearance and data are preserved exactly

stem: A defence supplier runs a control system tied to specialised on-site hardware. A regulator requires the equipment to stay inside the supplier's own facility for the next several years. The rest of its applications are moving to Google Cloud. What is the right migration decision for this control system?

choices.text: Retire it now, because anything that cannot move to the cloud has no place in a modern organization
Retain it where it is for now, and revisit the decision when the constraint changes
Rehost it in the cloud immediately, because the regulator's rule applies only to hardware that is out of warranty
Reimagine it as a new cloud product, because only a complete redesign is allowed to leave the facility

stem: A retailer must leave its leased data center within three months. Its main order system runs on VMs, works well, and the vendor-supported software cannot be changed. The team accepts that the cloud benefits will be limited at first. Which approach fits, and what is the trade-off?

choices.text: Rehost (lift and shift), which moves it fastest with the fewest changes, but it will not yet use cloud-native capabilities fully
Refactor, which rewrites the code for the cloud and gives the most benefit, but it takes the longest and needs changes to the code
Reimagine, which creates a new business model, but it requires that the vendor-supported software be modified first
Replatform onto serverless, which removes all servers, but it is the slowest approach because every VM is rebuilt by hand

stem: A publisher runs its content site on VMs with a self-managed database. The code is stable and staff do not want to rewrite it, but the team spends many hours on patching and backups. They move the site mostly as is, but switch the database to a managed Google Cloud database service. Which migration approach is this?

choices.text: Retire, because the self-managed database was switched off and the whole workload was decommissioned
Rehost, because the site was moved to Google Cloud with no changes of any kind to its parts
Reimagine, because using a managed database changes the publisher's business model
Replatform, because one targeted improvement was made while the application code stayed the same

stem: A ticketing company's monolithic application slows down every time a popular event goes on sale, and one change requires redeploying the whole system. Leadership approves a project to rewrite it as independent services that scale separately. Which migration approach is this?

choices.text: Retain, because the company keeps the same application and only adds new tools to monitor it
Replatform, because the existing application is moved to a managed database without any code changes
Refactor, because the application's code and architecture are modified to take advantage of cloud capabilities
Rehost, because the code is moved to Google Cloud and is run exactly as it ran in the data center

stem: A national insurer has moved its claims system to the cloud. It now wants to rethink the whole claims experience: customers submit photos, an AI agent drafts the assessment, and adjusters review exceptions, with new services built around the company's data. Which migration term describes this ambition?

choices.text: Retain, which keeps the existing process in place so that adjusters continue to do each step manually
Reimagine, which uses cloud and AI capabilities to rethink how the process and the business work
Rehost, which moves the existing claims process unchanged into virtual machines on Google Cloud
Retire, which removes the claims system so that customers file claims without any insurer system

stem: Three workloads were assessed. Workload 1 is a vendor package that cannot be modified and must leave a data center next quarter. Workload 2 is a core customer app whose monolithic design blocks growth and that has a funded modernization budget. Workload 3 is an internal tool that duplicates a newer company system. Which assignment of approaches is the best fit?

choices.text: Workload 1 rehost, workload 2 refactor, workload 3 retire
Workload 1 retire, workload 2 retain, workload 3 refactor
Workload 1 reimagine, workload 2 retire, workload 3 rehost
Workload 1 refactor, workload 2 rehost, workload 3 replatform

stem: Before approving a migration plan, a CFO asks what the assessment phase should deliver to make the plan reliable. Which TWO outputs are most useful? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A guarantee that every workload will cost less in the cloud than it does today, whichever approach is used
A list of every workload with its owner, its dependencies on other systems and its current usage
A commitment to rewrite every application as microservices, so that the portfolio is consistent
A decision that no workload will be retired or retained, so that the scope is fully predictable
A recommended migration approach per workload, based on its complexity, business value and constraints

stem: Two years after a lift and shift of its VMs, a logistics company says it has not seen the agility or cost gains it expected from the cloud. Which TWO explanations are the most likely? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Google Cloud does not offer features that allow existing applications to be modernized after they are moved
Rehost migrations always lose data, so the company has had to repeat its work several times
The workloads were moved with minimal change, so they do not yet use cloud-native features such as autoscaling or managed services
Lift and shift automatically converts every application to serverless, which then disables cost controls
The VMs are probably sized and run as they were in the data center, so capacity is still fixed rather than elastic

stem: A software company wants developers to build an application once and run it in the same way on a laptop, in testing and in production, with less overhead than starting a full virtual machine per copy. Which technology addresses this?

choices.text: Containers, which package an application with its dependencies and share the host operating system's kernel
Spot VMs, which are discounted machines that can be reclaimed and do not change how software is packaged
Dedicated hardware, which gives each application its own physical server so that no two versions can conflict
Load balancers, which spread requests across servers but do not package software or its dependencies

stem: An online retailer's single large application handles search, cart, payments and recommendations. A defect in recommendations has forced a full redeployment of the whole system twice this quarter. The team wants each function to be developed, deployed and scaled by its own small team. Which architecture style addresses this?

choices.text: A single bigger virtual machine, which adds capacity but leaves the one deployable unit unchanged
A backup and recovery architecture, which copies data to a second location to guard against outages
A monolithic architecture, which keeps all functions in one deployable unit so that they can change together
A microservices architecture, in which an application is split into small, independently deployable services

stem: A small team builds an app that processes photo uploads in occasional bursts: many in a few minutes and then none for hours. It wants to pay only while code is running and never manage servers. Which compute model fits?

choices.text: An on-premises server sized for the largest burst, to avoid any dependence on the cloud provider
A self-managed Kubernetes cluster, so the team can tune the nodes that process each upload
Serverless computing, in which the provider allocates and scales resources on demand and bills for actual use
Dedicated VMs left running around the clock, so capacity for the largest burst is always available

stem: A research institute runs a nightly genome-processing batch job. The job can be restarted from checkpoints, finishes within hours, and has no strict deadline. The institute wants the lowest compute cost. What is the trade-off of using Spot VMs?

choices.text: They cost much less as they use spare capacity, but Google can reclaim them, so the job must tolerate it
They cost the same as regular VMs, but they are the only type that can run batch jobs at night
They cost more than regular VMs, but they are never interrupted and so suit any deadline-bound job
They cost less because they are slower hardware, and they are guaranteed to run until a job completes

stem: A company has packaged dozens of services as containers. Operators now struggle to keep the right number of copies running, restart those that fail, roll out new versions without downtime and spread them over many machines. Which technology automates this container management?

choices.text: A virtual private network, which encrypts traffic between the offices and the cloud
A relational database, which stores the records the services produce and can keep them consistent
A content delivery network, which caches static content near users to shorten page load times
Kubernetes, an open source system that orchestrates the deployment, scaling and management of containers

stem: A ticket-selling site sees traffic rise tenfold within minutes when sales open, then fall again. In the past it bought hardware for the peak and paid for it all year. Which feature lets the site match capacity to demand automatically in the cloud?

choices.text: Rehosting, which moves the application to another data center before each sale
Autoscaling, which adds resources when demand rises and removes them when it drops
Retaining, which keeps a fixed amount of capacity running so that costs stay predictable
Data warehousing, which stores historical ticket sales so that they can be analyzed later

stem: A media company runs the same web application on many servers in several zones. Visitors sometimes get errors because one server is overloaded while others sit idle, and a failed server still receives traffic. What does a load balancer add?

choices.text: It converts the application into microservices so that each function runs on a different server
It distributes incoming requests across healthy servers, improving availability and use of capacity
It copies the application's data to a second region so that a backup exists if the first is lost
It encrypts the data stored on every server so that a stolen disk cannot be read

stem: A mid-sized company runs its own databases, patching and backups, and its small IT team spends most of its week on this routine upkeep rather than on projects that serve customers. Which approach most directly frees that time?

choices.text: Moving the same self-managed databases to larger virtual machines, to give them more headroom for growth
Buying more powerful servers, so that the routine maintenance tasks finish more quickly each week
Hiring an additional team to take over the maintenance, so that the existing staff are not involved
Using managed services, in which Google operates the underlying infrastructure and handles tasks such as patching and backups

stem: A company is choosing among VMs, containers on Kubernetes and serverless for different applications. Which TWO statements describe the trade-offs correctly? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Serverless gives the provider most of the operations, but offers less control over the underlying environment than VMs
Kubernetes removes all operations work, because the applications scale and update themselves without any configuration
VMs give the least control and the least operational effort, because Google patches the guest operating system
Serverless always costs the least, because it is cheaper than any other model for steady, constantly busy workloads
VMs give the most control over the operating system, but the company carries more work to patch, size and scale them

stem: A newly hired board adviser asks the CIO of a manufacturer for a one-sentence definition of "cloud" that a non-technical director would accept. Which definition is the most accurate?

choices.text: A software license that lets a company copy its internal applications onto an unlimited number of employee laptops for offline use by its staff
A long-term hosting contract in which a provider reserves specific physical servers for one customer and bills a fixed fee regardless of use
Computing resources such as storage and servers delivered on demand as services over the internet, with no self-managed hardware and pay-for-use billing
A private network of servers that a company buys, installs and operates in its own data centers, with capacity fixed at the level of the original purchase

stem: A marketing team used a generative AI tool to draft a promotional email. The head of digital now wants a system that, given the goal "raise sign-ups for the spring campaign", plans the steps, sends the emails through the company's marketing tools, watches the results and adjusts the plan on its own with little human intervention. Which term describes this system, and how does it differ from the earlier tool?

choices.text: A data warehouse, because it stores every campaign record in one place for analysts to query, where generative AI alone has no access to any stored information
Business intelligence, because it summarizes past campaign results in dashboards for people to read, where generative AI alone drafts the text of each email
Agentic AI, because agents use a language model to plan and act in other systems toward a goal, where generative AI alone creates content from a prompt
Agentic AI, because it removes people from all decisions permanently, where generative AI alone can only be used inside a single spreadsheet or document

stem: A retailer's CFO hears the CIO say that the company will "modernize its infrastructure" as the first step of its cloud program. The CFO asks what "infrastructure" refers to in this plan. Which description is correct?

choices.text: The foundational resources applications run on, such as servers (compute), storage and networking, in a company data center or from a cloud provider
The reports and dashboards that managers read each morning, since infrastructure means the output of analytics and the charts built from sales data
The set of company policies that decide which employees may approve purchases and sign contracts, independent of any technology the company uses
Only the customer-facing mobile app and website, because infrastructure means whatever shoppers see and touch when they browse and place an order

stem: A regional bank has moved its data center servers to a cloud provider with no change to its products, processes or customer channels. A new executive says the bank has "completed its digital transformation". Which response best reflects how Google Cloud defines digital transformation?

choices.text: Yes, because digital transformation means any migration of hardware to the cloud, whatever happens to products, processes and customer channels afterward
Yes, because digital transformation is complete once the number of physical servers owned by the company reaches zero, whatever else may have changed
Not yet, because digital transformation is finished only when every employee has been replaced by AI agents that handle all of the customer-facing work
Not yet, because transformation changes business processes, culture and customer experience, and moving servers alone does not redesign how the bank works

stem: A health-technology company wants to build its data platform on Kubernetes, a project whose source code is published for anyone to inspect, modify and share under a license that allows this. A board member asks what "open source" means for the company in business terms. Which answer is correct?

choices.text: The software runs only on hardware owned by the company, because its code cannot legally be placed on a cloud provider's servers or services
The source code is public, so anyone can inspect, modify and distribute it, a community can contribute and the company avoids dependence on one vendor
The software is always free of charge to run in production, and the company cannot pay anyone for support, hosting or managed services around it
The software has been certified by an international standards body, and every vendor must implement it in exactly the same way in every product

stem: A logistics company's systems must exchange shipment data with partners that use different vendors' software. The architect proposes that every system follow a publicly documented specification that any vendor can implement. What is this called, and what business benefit does it bring?

choices.text: A private cloud, which keeps shipment data inside one data center so that partners and outside systems cannot reach it or exchange it
An open standard, which lets different vendors' products work together and makes it easier to switch suppliers without rebuilding every integration
An open standard, which guarantees that all partners will use the same cloud provider, the same pricing model and the same support contract
A proprietary format, which locks every partner into one supplier so that the logistics company controls all exchanges between the parties involved

stem: A toy retailer sells most of its products in the eight weeks before the holidays. Every year it buys enough servers for that peak, and the servers sit mostly idle for the rest of the year. The retailer is considering the cloud. Which benefit most directly addresses this problem?

choices.text: Data residency, because the retailer chooses the country where each customer's order records are stored during the busy season
Open standards, because every vendor's server model follows the same published specification and can be connected into the retailer's own racks
Scalability, because capacity can rise for the seasonal peak and fall afterwards, so the retailer stops buying hardware sized for the busiest weeks
Vendor consolidation, because the retailer can reduce the number of suppliers on its approved list to exactly one

stem: A software company's finance lead complains that the company spends heavily on servers that must be sized for unexpected growth, while its IT staff spend most of their time on hardware upkeep. A cloud adviser says moving to the cloud improves cost-effectiveness. Which statement explains this benefit?

choices.text: The company avoids all spending on technology because the provider covers application development and staff costs as well as the infrastructure
The company pays a fixed annual fee for a fixed pool of servers, so its monthly costs never change, whatever demand does in a given month
The company keeps its servers but receives a rebate from the provider for each server that stays idle during the year, so the bill falls
The company pays only for the resources it uses, avoids overbuilding capacity, and can move staff from hardware upkeep to more strategic work

stem: A consumer-goods company needs a pilot environment for a new loyalty app. In its data center, ordering servers, receiving them, finding rack space and configuring them takes months. Leadership wants the team to test the idea within days and shut it down if the idea fails. Which cloud benefits does this describe?

choices.text: Agility and speed, because resources are available on demand without a procurement cycle, so teams can experiment and reach the market sooner
Data sovereignty, because the pilot will be restricted to one country by a legal decision that is made after the first tests have begun
Vendor neutrality, because the company's servers will be interchangeable with those of its competitors during the pilot and after it is over
Capital ownership, because the pilot servers become permanent assets on the balance sheet as soon as the test starts and are kept for years

stem: A consulting firm has employees in many countries who work from client sites, home and airports on different devices. Management wants every employee to reach the firm's applications securely from wherever there is an internet connection, and wants to resize capacity as projects start and end. Which cloud benefit is the firm mainly looking for?

choices.text: Permanence, because the capacity purchased for the first project must stay unchanged for the full life of the contract in all cases
Flexibility, because services can be accessed from anywhere with an internet connection and scaled up or down as needs change
Isolation, because applications can be reached only from computers inside the firm's headquarters building and never from outside it
Standardization, because every employee will be required to use the same single device model from the same location every working day

stem: A retailer's security chief doubts that a small in-house team can protect customer data better than a cloud provider can. A consultant lists what the cloud adds to security. Which TWO statements about cloud security are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Cloud providers cannot offer encryption, so customers must buy a separate product to protect data at rest
Security risks are identical in every environment, so the choice of provider has no influence on a company's risk
A cloud provider's security teams are widely regarded as top experts in the field, and the customer benefits from their work
Moving to the cloud makes the customer's security team unnecessary, because the provider alone is responsible for every control
Cloud security is generally recognized as stronger than that of typical enterprise data centers because of the depth and breadth of the mechanisms that providers build in

stem: A streaming company plans to launch in several new countries. It wants viewers on different continents to get fast, reliable playback, and it wants the service to keep running if one data center has a problem. Which cloud benefit is the company relying on?

choices.text: Global reach and high availability, because resources run in many locations close to users and a single failure does not stop the service
Manual failover, because engineers fly to a backup site to carry out repairs and restart the service whenever the main data center fails
Local-only licensing, because the service can legally run only in the first country where it was launched and in no other market
Single-site simplicity, because all viewers connect to one data center in the home country, which keeps the design easy to manage and cheap to run

stem: An insurer has years of claims records, call transcripts and photos spread across aging on-premises storage systems that are almost full. Analysts cannot easily query them together, and leaders want better forecasts. Which cloud benefit addresses this need?

choices.text: Network isolation, because disconnecting all systems from each other prevents data from being combined incorrectly by the analytics teams
Paper archiving, because printing records removes the need to analyze them and so reduces forecasting error in the claims department
Hardware nostalgia, because keeping the old storage systems unchanged guarantees that analysts will see more data over time and in one place
Data-driven insights, because the cloud stores large volumes of data accessibly and offers analytics tools that help the insurer spot trends and decide

stem: Two-thirds of a media company's IT budget and staff time goes to patching servers, replacing disks and managing data center power, leaving little capacity for features that would differentiate its streaming service. How does adopting cloud services address this concern?

choices.text: The company keeps all of its maintenance duties, but a cloud provider supplies a faster set of tools for carrying out each of them every month
The provider takes control of the company's product roadmap, so decisions about streaming features are made by the provider's own staff
The provider runs the underlying infrastructure and supplies innovations as services, so the company can focus on differentiating products and return on investment
The company's engineers must learn the provider's hardware repair procedures, so their time moves from its data centers to the provider's data centers

stem: A board is reviewing why companies pursue digital transformation. Which TWO statements describe primary drivers that motivate organizations to transform? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Regulators forbid all use of data, so companies transform in order to stop collecting it
Customers and markets change quickly, so the company needs the agility to meet new expectations and compete with digital-native rivals
Existing contracts forbid the purchase of any new technology, so transformation is a way to avoid change
Employees dislike new tools, so leadership transforms in order to hold on to existing processes for as long as possible and avoid training costs
Large volumes of data from many sources can be turned into insight, so the company seeks smarter analytics and AI to inform decisions

stem: A manufacturer bought a modern cloud platform and trained its engineers, but a year later teams still run old manual approval processes, business units keep separate data and middle managers resist changes to their roles. Leadership asks what the main obstacle is. Which diagnosis is most accurate?

choices.text: Excessive openness, because open standards prevent teams from agreeing on shared processes and force each unit to keep its own manual approvals
Insufficient server capacity, because the cloud platform cannot handle the manufacturer's volume of transactions during its busiest production periods
A shortage of electricity, because cloud platforms cannot run in more than one building and the manufacturer's building has limited power supply
Cultural and organizational resistance, because people, processes and culture must change along with the technology and these were left unchanged

stem: A mid-sized retailer decides to postpone cloud adoption for three more years and continue to run its own data center. Which TWO risks does this decision create? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Competitors that use cloud, data and AI can launch products and respond to customers faster, so the retailer may lose market share
The retailer's data center will automatically become a public cloud region operated by a provider
The retailer will lose all of its existing customers on the day the three years begin, because on-premises systems stop working
The retailer will be unable to use any other vendor's software, because cloud adoption is a prerequisite for software licensing
The retailer must keep paying for hardware, space and staff sized for peak demand, and its capacity may still be unable to follow growth

stem: A company already runs applications on another provider and on premises, and its CTO fears that choosing Google Cloud will make the company dependent on one more vendor. Which Google Cloud approach speaks to this concern?

choices.text: A closed platform in which only Google's proprietary formats are supported, to give the customer a single consistent way of working across all of its systems
Multicloud solutions built on open-source technologies such as Kubernetes, so workloads can run and move across clouds and computing environments
A rule that customers must retire every other provider within a year of signing, to simplify administration and give one supplier a single point of contact
A guarantee that no application will ever need to be changed, whatever the platform it is moved to and however different the target environment may be

stem: A bank wants to build AI models on its own customer-transaction data. Its data team currently exports data from the warehouse into separate machine learning tools, which is slow and makes the data harder to govern. Which Google Cloud differentiator addresses this?

choices.text: A requirement that all data be printed and re-entered by hand before any model can see it, to ensure accuracy of the training examples used by the bank
A pre-built model that works for every industry without using any of the bank's data, which removes the need for any data governance or review
A separate AI laboratory in another country, where the bank's data is sent to be used for training other customers' models as well as its own
An AI-ready data platform, where the data estate (such as BigQuery), model development on Agent Platform and accelerators work together in one place

stem: A research start-up trains large models and worries about two things: being stuck with one type of accelerator chip, and paying more than necessary for jobs that can wait. Which TWO features of Google Cloud's AI Hypercomputer address these worries? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The choice of both TPUs and GPUs, supported by open-source frameworks, so teams can use the best accelerator without being tied to one type
A guarantee that every training job will complete at the same cost, regardless of when it is scheduled
A single fixed accelerator type that every customer must use, bought up front for a commitment period that cannot be changed or shortened later
A requirement to rewrite all training code in a proprietary language for each new generation of hardware, with a new support contract for each
Flexible consumption models, such as Spot VMs and Dynamic Workload Scheduler, that lower the cost of fault-tolerant or flexible-start jobs

stem: A global gaming company wants a consistent experience for players on several continents. An executive asks which TWO characteristics of Google's global network infrastructure help with this. (Select TWO)

choices.text: A design that allows traffic only within a single country, so no player ever connects to another continent
A requirement for customers to build and operate their own undersea cables before launching a game in a new region
Network edge locations close to users, so workloads are processed near the player and responses come back quickly
A network that routes all traffic through one central city, so every player is the same distance from a single data center that serves the whole world
A private global fiber network connecting over 200 countries, which Google says minimizes latency and security risks for enterprise applications

stem: A telecom company is evaluating an AI customer-support agent. The vendor says the agent is "agentic", and the company's COO asks what the agent should be able to do to deserve that label. Which capability description fits agentic AI?

choices.text: It prints a list of frequently asked questions whenever a customer types a keyword, and never changes its answers or looks at the customer's account
It forwards every customer message to a human agent without reading it, then records which agent answered and how long the customer waited
It gathers data from systems, reasons about the problem with a language model, plans steps, takes actions such as updating an account, and learns from results
It stores recordings of customer calls for future auditing and quality review, but cannot respond to the customer or act during the call
